workingTitle: ALMA finds a gentle warp in the planet-forming ring around CQ Tau
freshness: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal; arXiv preprint submitted October 26, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: The team combined three archival ALMA Band 6 datasets to map 1.3-millimeter dust emission around the roughly 10-million-year-old star CQ Tau at an effective resolution of 7.8 by 6.3 astronomical units.
Ellipse fits to the bright ring show that its apparent orientation changes with radius, while a single coplanar ring model fails to reproduce the data.
A simple warped-ring model, with the tilt decreasing from about 4 degrees at 20 astronomical units to about 1 degree at 60 astronomical units, broadly reproduces the observed trend.
An inclined companion could create the warp, but no companion has been detected and the paper does not rule out other histories such as a stellar flyby or past infall.
